**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Leaf (upper surface shown)
- **Key features**: Numerous small, scattered tan-to-orange/yellow spots uniformly distributed across the leaf surface; spots are small and dot-like; a few larger brown lesion holes also present; overall leaf has a slightly mottled yellowish-green cast

**Candidate narrowing:**

- **Soybean rust**: Small tan to brown and brick red spots on leaves, pustules on lower leaf surface — matches the scattered small tan/orange dots well
- **Septoria brown spot**: Small, irregular dark brown lesions on both surfaces, lower canopy — lesions are typically darker and more irregular
- **Downy mildew**: Yellow spots on upper surface, gray tufts below — possible but spots here are more tan/orange than bright yellow
- **Frogeye leaf spot**: Gray centers with reddish-brown borders — lesions are larger and more distinct

The pattern — numerous very small, uniformly scattered tan-to-orange dots across the upper leaf surface — is most consistent with early **Soybean rust** lesions. The spots have the characteristic coloration (tan to brick-red) and distribution starting on the leaf surface, consistent with early uredinia development. Septoria lesions tend to be darker brown and coalesce more; downy mildew spots are more yellow-green.
